question:
Tamara has three rows of two \(6\)-feet by \(2\)-feet flower beds in her garden. The beds are separated and also surrounded by \(1\)-foot-wide walkways, as shown on the diagram. What is the total area of the walkways, in square feet?

[Figure 1](figures/2017_AMC_10A_Q03_question_fig1.svg)
solution:
The walkways occupy everything inside the outside rectangle except the six flower beds, so subtracting the beds avoids counting walkway intersections separately.

Across a row, there are two \(6\)-foot beds and three \(1\)-foot walkways: one at each outside edge and one between the beds. The total length is
\[
2\cdot6+3\cdot1=15\text{ feet}.
\]
Across the three rows, there are three \(2\)-foot bed widths and four \(1\)-foot walkways, giving
\[
3\cdot2+4\cdot1=10\text{ feet}.
\]
The outside rectangle therefore has area \(15\cdot10=150\) square feet. The six beds occupy \(6(6\cdot2)=72\) square feet. Hence the walkway area is
\[
150-72=\boxed{78}\text{ square feet},
\]
choice B.
